title: Topic Modeling of Greek Parliament Proceedings using Natural Language Processing
description: This presentation details the methodology used to analyze a large corpus of Greek Parliament data to extract dynamic themes. The process involves digitizing, annotating, and preprocessing the session minutes before applying both TF-IDF and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) to identify key topics.
summary: The work focuses on analyzing data from the Greek Parliament, utilizing nearly 26 years of plenary sessions containing over 1 million unique speeches. The data was first digitized, normalized, and transformed into a structured XML format. In the preparation phase, the session texts were enriched with detailed annotations, including speaker details, and the input was preprocessed by removing stop words and focusing only on content words (nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs). This first phase yielded 283 window-based topics. A second phase applied the NMF model, using topic coherence to determine the number of dynamic topics, resulting in 90 dynamic topics. The study further used Word2Vec embeddings on the full corpus to extract dynamic topics, providing examples such as Topic 79, where the word 'memorandum' is highly associated with themes like negotiation, the Eurozone, and monetary negotiation.

title: Dynamic Topic Modeling of Political Speech Data for Plenary Session Analysis
description: This work utilizes dynamic topic modeling, inspired by Green Growth, to identify and monitor evolving thematic topics within Greek Parliament data. The methodology involves organizing data into monthly windows, applying dynamic NMF, and creating an interactive visualization platform for detailed exploration of political activity.
summary: The research employs a six-step workflow—data collection through organization, preprocessing, and topic modeling—to analyze political discourse. Data was organized into one-month temporal windows to monitor the dynamics of topics across different periods. A dynamic Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) approach is used to identify and group semantically similar topics within these time windows. The results are presented on a visualization platform that allows users to explore these dynamic topics by viewing descriptive terms, associated parties, regions, frequencies, and satisfaction metrics. Furthermore, users can search for related topics or explore specific windows to understand what events (e.g., many politicians, specific topics) occurred during particular time periods, providing deep insight into plenary sessions.

title: Analyzing Parliamentary Data for Political and Policy Agenda Monitoring
description: This work involves digitizing and analyzing minutes of parliamentary proceedings to create a structured text corpus. A platform is developed to enable insightful navigation of this data, tracking the evolution of political agendas, and assessing the contributions of political parties and electoral districts.
summary: The core contribution of this work is twofold: first, digitizing and processing the minutes of plenary sessions from Greece over the last 26 years into a structured corpus suitable for NLP and text mining. Second, a platform is created that allows users to navigate this data based on topic modeling analysis, enabling exploration of speeches by topic, time, and satisfaction, alongside charts detailing the contribution of political parties and electoral districts to specific topics. This provides valuable information for stakeholders to more perceptively monitor the political and policy agenda. Future plans include evaluating extracted topics, conducting interdisciplinary research with political scientists to examine specific dynamic topics (e.g., the refugee crisis) and comparing them internationally, and applying sentiment analysis and quotation extraction for further insights.
